entities.summary:
Hywel ab Edwin was a monarch of the Kingdom of Powys in the 11th century, playing a pivotal role in shaping the region's governance and politics during the Classical era. Their ascension to the throne in 1009 marked the beginning of a new era of stability and prosperity for the kingdom, which was characterized by a complex web of alliances and rivalries with neighboring powers.

The legacy of Hywel ab Edwin can be seen in the continued influence of the Kingdom of Powys on the politics of the region, as well as the lasting impact of their policies on the development of the Welsh language and culture. The precise dates of their birth and death are unknown, but it is widely acknowledged that they died in 1044, marking the end of an era in the Kingdom of Powys.

Hywel ab Edwin's story is a testament to the enduring power of leadership and the importance of understanding the complexities of human history. Their work continues to captivate historians and scholars today, offering a unique window into the world of the 11th century.
